questions.q: Find the complex conjugate of $z=5-3i$, and compute $z\bar{z}$.
Simplify $\dfrac{2+i}{3-2i}$ by multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator.
The graph shows several complex numbers plotted as points on the Argand diagram (real part on the horizontal axis, imaginary part on the vertical axis).
parts: Read off the complex number plotted closest to the point $(3,2)$ in Cartesian (real, imaginary) form.
Find the modulus of the complex number plotted at $(-3,-3)$.
answers: The point $(3,2)$ corresponds to the complex number $3+2i$.
The point $(-3,-3)$ corresponds to $-3-3i$, with modulus $|-3-3i|=\sqrt{(-3)^2+(-3)^2}=\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: Solve $x^2+4x+13=0$, giving your answer in the form $a+bi$.
One root of a quadratic equation with real coefficients is $2-5i$. State the other root, and find the quadratic equation.
questions.answer: Since coefficients are real, complex roots occur in conjugate pairs, so the other root is $2+5i$. Sum of roots $=4$; product of roots $=(2-5i)(2+5i)=4+25=29$. Equation: $x^2-4x+29=0$.

questions.q: Find real numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $(x+yi)(2-i)=8+i$.
questions.answer: Expand: $(x+yi)(2-i)=2x-xi+2yi-yi^2=2x+y+(2y-x)i$. Equate real and imaginary parts: $2x+y=8$ and $2y-x=1$. From the first, $y=8-2x$. Substitute: $2(8-2x)-x=1$, so $16-4x-x=1$, $16-5x=1$, $x=3$. Then $y=8-6=2$. So $x=3$, $y=2$.

Simplify $i^{23}$, using the fact that powers of $i$ cycle with period 4 ($i^1=i$, $i^2=-1$, $i^3=-i$, $i^4=1$).

sections.heading: The geometry of complex conjugates and reflections

questions.q: Explain, in terms of the Argand diagram, what geometric transformation taking the conjugate of a complex number represents, and state the conjugate of $z=-4+7i$.
questions.answer: Taking the complex conjugate reflects the point representing $z$ across the real axis (the horizontal axis) on the Argand diagram — the real part stays the same while the sign of the imaginary part flips. The conjugate of $z=-4+7i$ is $\bar{z}=-4-7i$.

questions.q: If $z=a+bi$, express $\text{Re}(z)$ and $\text{Im}(z)$ in terms of $z$ and $\bar{z}$.
questions.answer: Since $z+\bar{z}=(a+bi)+(a-bi)=2a$, we get $\text{Re}(z)=a=\dfrac{z+\bar{z}}{2}$. Since $z-\bar{z}=(a+bi)-(a-bi)=2bi$, we get $\text{Im}(z)=b=\dfrac{z-\bar{z}}{2i}$.

sections.heading: Solving simultaneous equations with complex numbers

questions.q: Solve the simultaneous equations $z_1+z_2=5+3i$ and $z_1-z_2=1+7i$ for complex numbers $z_1$ and $z_2$.
questions.answer: Adding the two equations: $2z_1=6+10i$, so $z_1=3+5i$. Subtracting: $2z_2=4-4i$, so $z_2=2-2i$.

questions.q: Given that $z=2+3i$ is a root of $z^3-5z^2+17z-13=0$ (a cubic with real coefficients), state the second complex root immediately (without further calculation), then find the third (real) root.
questions.answer: Since the cubic has real coefficients, complex roots occur in conjugate pairs, so $z=2-3i$ is also a root immediately. The two complex roots multiply to $(2+3i)(2-3i)=4+9=13$ and sum to $4$, so together they correspond to the quadratic factor $z^2-4z+13$. Dividing the cubic by this factor: $z^3-5z^2+17z-13\div(z^2-4z+13)=z-1$. So the third root is $z=1$.

sections.heading: Loci and regions in the complex plane

questions.q: Describe, geometrically, the locus of points $z$ satisfying $|z-3-4i|=5$, and state its center and radius.
questions.answer: The equation $|z-(3+4i)|=5$ describes all points $z$ whose distance from the fixed point $3+4i$ equals $5$. This is a circle centered at $(3,4)$ with radius $5$.

questions.q: Find the two square roots of $z=5+12i$ algebraically, by writing $\sqrt{5+12i}=a+bi$ and solving the resulting simultaneous equations $a^2-b^2=5$ and $2ab=12$.
questions.answer: From $2ab=12$, $b=\dfrac{6}{a}$. Substitute into $a^2-b^2=5$: $a^2-\dfrac{36}{a^2}=5$, so $a^4-5a^2-36=0$. Let $u=a^2$: $u^2-5u-36=0$, factoring $(u-9)(u+4)=0$, so $u=9$ (rejecting the negative root since $a^2\geq0$). Then $a=\pm3$, and $b=\dfrac{6}{a}=\pm2$ (matching sign). Roots: $z=3+2i$ or $z=-3-2i$.

questions.q: Prove that $|z_1z_2|=|z_1||z_2|$ for any complex numbers $z_1=a+bi$ and $z_2=c+di$, by expanding both sides directly.
questions.answer: $z_1z_2=(a+bi)(c+di)=(ac-bd)+(ad+bc)i$. So $|z_1z_2|^2=(ac-bd)^2+(ad+bc)^2=a^2c^2-2abcd+b^2d^2+a^2d^2+2abcd+b^2c^2=a^2c^2+b^2d^2+a^2d^2+b^2c^2=a^2(c^2+d^2)+b^2(c^2+d^2)=(a^2+b^2)(c^2+d^2)$. Also $|z_1|^2|z_2|^2=(a^2+b^2)(c^2+d^2)$, matching exactly. Since both sides are non-negative, taking square roots gives $|z_1z_2|=|z_1||z_2|$.

questions.q: Given $z=x+yi$ satisfies $z^2=\bar{z}$, find all complex solutions $z$.
questions.answer: $z^2=(x+yi)^2=(x^2-y^2)+2xyi$, and $\bar{z}=x-yi$. Equating real and imaginary parts: $x^2-y^2=x$ and $2xy=-y$. From the second equation, either $y=0$ or $x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$. Case $y=0$: $x^2=x$, so $x=0$ or $x=1$, giving $z=0$ or $z=1$. Case $x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$: $\dfrac{1}{4}-y^2=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, so $y^2=\dfrac{3}{4}$, giving $y=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, so $z=-\dfrac{1}{2}\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$. All solutions: $z=0,\ 1,\ -\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i,\ -\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$.
